title: Resolve schedule_ref to its declared cadence (remove silent 7-day fallback)
increment: Resolve source.schedule_ref against the loaded ScheduleSet, derive a staleness window from the cron (window = 2x nominal cadence), store the derived compact window in Source.schedule, and fail closed (reject at the resolution seam, naming the ref) on any unresolvable/underivable reference. Explicitly do NOT widen parse_schedule_window to accept the ref name strings.
acceptance: cron_to_cadence derives 1h/1d/6h/7d from the real cron expressions; returns None (fail-closed) on inputs it cannot expand.
resolve_schedule_window raises an actionable error naming the offending ref when the ref is absent from the ScheduleSet or the cron cannot yield a window; it never returns a 7-day default.
sync stores the derived compact window (e.g. '2d','2h') in Source.schedule so reconcile.py and publisher.py resolve real windows without change.
parse_schedule_window still handles hourly/daily/compact unchanged (precision preserved).
Deterministic before/after impact table over the real committed configs: source -> ref -> 7d vs new window -> flip age-band; all changes are fresh->stale (tighter).
Full pytest suite green with reported collected counts; ruff check and ruff format --check clean.
derivation_decision: window = 2 x nominal cadence (min consecutive cron fire gap). Rationale: tolerate exactly one missed/jittered scan cycle; 1x is too tight and would wrongly withhold correct free offers, a defect of equal severity to wrongly publishing (unknown-is-better-than-guessed cuts both ways).
measurement_limit: Exact per-offer verdict flips require a live PostgreSQL DB; integration suite is DATABASE_URL-gated and skips in this Python-only env. Deterministic window/age-band table is provided instead.
